review_type: Read-only actual-pixel visual review of call screen PNGs

identity_verification.ci_run_id_provenance: Assigned artifact run identity supplied by parent reviewer; no remote CI query performed in this visual-only subtask

status_scope: Only rendering visible in the 101 listed PNGs; no end-to-end call behavior, hardware, release or installation approval is implied.

coverage.base_matrix: Five themes, light/dark, normal/audio/more/keypad, font scale 1.0/1.3
coverage.long_name_matrix: Five themes, dark, Hebrew/English long names, normal/audio, font scale 1.3
coverage.additional_case: Google Phone light English audio output with no Bluetooth device
coverage.review_method: Each call-01.png through call-26.png was opened using tools.view_image and forwarded using image(...); all occupied frames were actually inspected. The 480x854 frame crops were then checked byte-for-byte against the original PNG pixels, without rescaling. Original graphite dark More largefont was additionally opened directly.

checks.observation: No confirmed glyph clipping, overlapping text/control, missing control, unexpected blank frame, or off-screen end-call control was observed. Keypad digits, letters, star/hash/plus, panel close buttons, titles and route/More rows remain visible at both font scales.

Long names are visibly ellipsized within their available width and do not overlap avatar, phone number, timer or audio panel. Hebrew truncation appears at the visual left; English truncation appears at the visual right. Phone numbers remain readable.

checks.check: Native status/navigation bars and safe area
checks.observation: Native top time/status symbols and three-button navigation remain visible with appropriate light/dark contrast. End-call controls have visible separation from the navigation bar. No native-bar collision was observed.

The themes remain visually distinct: circular Samsung controls, Google Phone rounded trays with peach selected controls, outlined glass surfaces, HyperOS rectangular action cards, and Nothing monochrome/dotted surfaces with squared rows. Light/dark backgrounds and button/text contrast are coherent in these captures.

checks.check: End call and capability controls as rendered
checks.observation: Every frame shows an unobscured red/coral end-call control. Normal panels expose the theme-specific action arrangement; More sheets show New call/Hold rows, audio sheets show route choices/selection, and keypad sheets show all twelve keys. This establishes visible rendering only, not Telecom capability or action execution.
call-pixel-light-audio-english-no-bluetooth.png visibly shows Audio output, Speaker, selected Phone, More/Mute/Keypad, and end-call, with no Bluetooth/F901 choice.

non_blocking_observations.observation: The large Hebrew New call label uses visible ellipsis in the narrow normal-layout action slot; the icon and remaining label stay separate from adjacent controls.
More title has very tight right spacing against the graphite panel edge. Full title was visible, including on the directly reopened original dark largefont PNG; no confirmed clipping was found.

limitations: These call-layout PNGs are real Android renders driven by synthetic call/audio fixtures; they are not proof of a live Telecom connection or physical audio behavior.
No screenshot can establish touch hit area, actual mute/route/hold/add-call/DTMF/hang-up execution, lifecycle behavior, or accessibility announcement correctness.
Physical Jelly Star, SIM/carrier, audible microphone/speaker/Bluetooth, proximity/lock/OEM, full TalkBack and matching-key upgrade are NOT TESTED by this review.
The long-name fixtures cover dark normal/audio panels, not every light/keypad/More permutation.
release_blockers_and_accounting_from_par: Production business source bytes and production rows remain 0; native dataset check is the single known failing native test.
Native accounting is 34 tests: 33 pass, 1 fail; the functional PNG artifact has 237 PNGs, not the 241 originally planned.
Installed beta9 matching private signing key remains unavailable; in-place compatibility has not been proven.
